current.title: Developing Global Infrastructure to Study Political Polarization
current.blurb: This project develops measures, scales, and research protocols for studying political polarization across Latin America, extending earlier work conducted in the United States and Brazil.
current.credit: With Walter Sinnott-Armstrong and Paulo Boggio

current.title: Connecting, Advancing, and Nurturing Moral Psychology
current.blurb: This project supports a global scholarly community devoted to interdisciplinary moral psychology. It includes the International Society for Moral Psychology and a linked mentorship program for the next generation of moral psychologists.
current.credit: With John Doris, Valerie Tiberius, Santiago Amaya, Laura Niemi, and Shaun Nichols

past.title: Building Empathy for Depolarization in the United States and Brazil
past.blurb: A cross-cultural study of conversational interventions designed to mitigate affective polarization. The project developed new methods for comparing polarization and depolarization across cultures.

past.title: Global Moral Codes
past.blurb: A global experience-sampling study of everyday moral experiences involving approximately 3,000 participants across 15 countries.
past.credit: With William Jiménez-Leal and Santiago Amaya

past.title: Consciousness, Just in Time
past.blurb: A project validating measures of dynamic modes of thought and studying transitions between modes of thinking in virtual-reality environments.
past.credit: With Zac Irving and Caitlin Mills

past.title: Moral Psychology off the Rails
past.blurb: A project developing new measures and situations for studying moral judgment, with particular attention to non-Western and rural populations in Colombia.
past.credit: Based at the Universidad de los Andes, Bogotá

earlier: Earlier projects examined vigilance and self-control, mind-wandering and prospective memory, moral responsibility for omissions, and the relationship between mind-wandering and creativity.
